headline: Warm, dry weather through Friday, then cooler with light rain Saturday and more unsettled weather into early next week.
summary: High pressure builds over the Northwest through Friday. Skies are clearing, with highs in the upper 60s to low 70s Thursday and the mid 70s Friday. Forecasters note some Minor HeatRisk on both days, meaning the warmth could affect a small number of people who are especially sensitive to heat. Because the lower air is moist and winds are light, low cloud and possibly fog could form Thursday morning, though that is only a possibility. Winds from the east will get a little breezy in the Cascades and foothills Thursday night, with gusts of 25 to 30 mph. Humidity could fall to around 35 to 40% in the Cascades and southern Olympics Thursday, and to 35 to 45% more widely Friday. The weather turns over the weekend as the high weakens and a series of weak systems moves through. Saturday will likely bring rain during the day, mostly to the North Cascades, with only a few hundredths of an inch in the lowlands. Parts of the Seattle area may stay dry. Highs drop to the low 60s Saturday, a sharp fall from Friday's mid 70s. Sunday looks cooler and drier, with morning lows in the low 40s around Puget Sound and the mid 30s in the Cascade foothills. Cool, unsettled weather continues into early next week, with more chances for light rain, especially Tuesday. Forecasters will watch whether the offshore trough shifts its track, and they say the pattern after Tuesday is unclear because the models disagree. Seas on the coastal waters will build over the weekend.
changes: The early-morning forecast had a possible convergence-zone shower area and a Sunday-Monday system that might miss Washington. By evening, Saturday rain was described as mostly light and focused on the North Cascades, with Sunday cooler and drier, and the offshore track still being watched. Forecasters also added more detail on Thursday-Friday warmth, fog, and breezy east winds in the Cascades.
